scenario: [LNUL.4.9] — a `Time` written by `now()` answers `is Int` TRUE. Drives the libds TIME-TAG route specifically: rule `stamp` binds `now()` in a let and emits it into a `Time`-typed slot, so the stored value carries DS_RETE_VAL_TIME rather than DS_RETE_VAL_INT; rule `check` then reads that slot through the eval arm's IS_SUBJECT_INT case. Two rules because `now()` is let-RHS-only and a `where` cannot read a let, so the TIME tag has to be put into working memory by one activation and tested by another. Pins the arm at `rete/eval.c`'s DS_RETE_IS_INT: an arm that reads `v.kind == DS_RETE_VAL_INT` alone answers FALSE here. ONLY MEANINGFUL BESIDE LNUL.4.9l, which drives the other route into the same slot: this one cannot fail in Mercury (it has no separate write path to disagree about), and it is the pair that pins provenance-independence rather than either alone. fact_count 3 — Ping, Stamped, Marker.
rules_ds:
schema Ping scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

schema Stamped scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    stamp: Time mutable

schema Marker scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule stamp:
    Ping p
->
    let n = now()
    emit Stamped logical entity_id: p.entity_id stamp: n

rule check:
    Stamped s where s.stamp is Int
->
    emit Marker logical entity_id: s.entity_id
